title: Premature Custom Thread-Local Storage (TLS) Caching
pattern: Using OS-level or compiler-level Thread-Local Storage to store transient scratch vectors or local caches to avoid mutex or allocation overhead without profiling.
why_bad: The lookup overhead of thread-local variables (which involves operating-system-specific register swaps or segment pointer calculations) can easily exceed the cost of simple parameters or standard stack-allocated data. It also severely complicates testing, thread joining, and leaks memory if threads are created dynamically [111, 223].
detection: Excessive use of the `thread_local!` macro or `#[thread_local]` attributes to store state or collections that could simply be passed as function references or are uncontended.
counterexample: High-performance profiling tools, CPU counters, or random number generator states (`rand::ThreadRng`) where true per-thread independent isolation is required. `Contextual`.
fix: Pass mutable scratch buffers directly to functions as arguments (`&mut Vec<i32>`), allowing threads to manage allocations cleanly on the call stack.
